headline: High-risk shared-write orchestration and medium prompt/data/cascade risks; no direct evidence of a shared bridge beyond host files and APIs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can read/write the host working directory and parse stdin/stdout, while Agent B exposes a REST API surface. A shared filesystem or copied outputs could let attacker-controlled content from B be treated as instructions by A. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF agent_b outputs are copied into agent_a-readable files or stdin/stdout
IF agent_a treats file or stream content as trusted instructions
mitigations: Separate B outputs from A inputs with distinct directories
Prefix all B-derived text with a non-executable marker
Add a manual review step before A consumes B output
Disable automatic ingestion of API responses into A prompts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches developer-passed crew data and has broad network egress; Agent B also has broad network egress and a REST API surface. If they share a workspace or the same data class, either could transmit sensitive content off-host. No direct evidence shows a shared workspace, so this is inferred but still plausible enough for medium.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b are given the same sensitive workspace or prompt payload
IF either agent forwards that content through its network egress
mitigations: Keep sensitive inputs out of shared directories
Route B through a redacted test dataset
Disable outbound network for one agent during evaluation
Review outbound payloads for secrets before sending

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while Agent B exposes a REST API and is not runnable locally. There is no evidence of locking or coordination, so overlapping writes to shared resources remain plausible if the orchestrator connects them. Because the shared target is not documented, uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same host directory or shared artifact store
IF the orchestrator does not serialize access to those resources
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Add file locks around shared artifacts
Serialize write phases in the orchestrator
Use read-only mounts for one agent

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A is a multi-agent orchestration framework with shared memory, so its outputs can become inputs to downstream steps. Agent B is an observability/evaluation API surface, which could consume A-produced artifacts without verification. That creates a plausible cascade from A to B, but the exact handoff is undocumented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes artifacts or summaries produced by agent_a
IF no verification step checks A's outputs before B acts on them
mitigations: Insert a validation step between A and B
Require citations or schema checks on A outputs
Have B flag low-confidence inputs instead of acting on them
Log and diff A outputs before downstream use

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and list no explicit residency, certification, or retention constraints. Agent A handles developer-passed crew data and Agent B lists no data classes touched, so there is no documented compliance mismatch. The other agent is not cited beyond confirming the absence of a stated conflict.
conditions: IF either profile later adds regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII
IF a deployment policy imposes residency or retention rules not shown here
mitigations: Document the data classes before deployment
Confirm retention settings for any shared logs
Keep regulated data out of this pair until policies are explicit
